notes.budget: N = 10000 for every cell of every ladder and of the n-sweep; alpha in {0.01,0.05,0.10} evaluated from the same arrays.
notes.seeds: Within a ladder every rung (and every test) uses the same seed (common random numbers); within a scenario of the n-sweep every n uses the same seed. The Normal rung is shared by the skewness and kurtosis ladders, so their baselines are numerically identical.
notes.parents: Ladder parents are standardised to mean 0 and variance 1; all tests on the distributional ladders are scale-invariant, so alpha-hat is unaffected by the standardisation.
notes.archived_anchors: Anchor cells (Exp(1)-1 skew, raw t(5) heavy tail, 1:4 variance ratio, 1:2:3 imbalance, np_min = 2) are re-run with experiments.py itself in consistency_checks; the n-sweep uses standardised t(5) instead of raw t(5) (equivalent for scale-invariant tests).
code_findings: experiments.py mc_cochran_q ignores its `unbalanced` argument and run_study2 never passes it: the published T8 'unbalanced' cell is a re-run of its baseline (see severity_sweep.not_applicable).

experiments.py calls two different code paths for Fligner-Killeen: the balanced path builds normal scores of the pooled |x - group median| ranks with raw argsort ranks; the unbalanced path calls scipy.stats.fligner, which in scipy 1.16.3 uses the SAME normal scores but averages tied ranks. The paths therefore differ only in tie handling (each even-sized group contributes one exact tie pair, because its two central order statistics are equidistant from the sample median): over 10000 same-dataset replications the max |statistic difference| is 2.50e-05 at ns=50/50/50, 4.12e-06 at ns=50/100/150 and 1.08e-01 at ns=9/12/9 (small groups), while the rejection decision agrees for at least 99.92% of replications in every configuration and the T6 unbalanced anchor's archived and generic Wilson CIs overlap. See fligner_variant_probe.configurations.

The archived T3/T9 baseline scenarios use a uniform parent (dist='uniform' default) while T1/T2/T5/T6/T7/T10 use normal; the structural ladders keep that convention, the skewness/kurtosis ladders use a common N(0,1) baseline.

One of 37 archived anchor cells (T9 unbalanced) has Wilson CIs that do not overlap its generic re-run (0.0481 vs 0.0571, z=2.9); max absolute anchor difference over all 37 cells is 0.011, i.e. MC noise.
upstream_issues: core.py T11_kpss: critical_value() returns cvm_limit_ppf(alpha) (0.0366 at alpha=0.05) although reference_ppf() expects an upper-tail probability; the Cramer-von Mises 5% quantile is cvm_limit_ppf(0.95) = 0.4614. Under iid N(0,1) the wrong value gives a KPSS rejection rate of ~1.00, the correct one ~0.05. Every T11 record therefore carries both rates (alpha_hat and evaluation_override.rate_with_core_rule) and the two critical values. Reported to t1-new-tests; no other test is affected (scipy families use isf, hoeffding_z follows the upper-tail convention and calibrates correctly).
notes.publication_check: implementation_validation.published_table4_reproduction compares the archived re-run with the published Table 4 rates.
notes.structure: Structural ladders (variance ratio, imbalance) use each test's archived baseline parent (uniform for T3/T9, normal elsewhere); the skewness and kurtosis ladders use a common N(0,1) baseline for all tests.

consistency_check_summary.framing: Each of the 37 archived-vs-generic anchor cells is an independent two-sample comparison of rejection rates at N=10,000. The largest discrepancy is |z| = 2.85, a two-sided event of probability 0.0044 per comparison; across 37 comparisons the expected number of such events under pure Monte Carlo noise is 0.16. Observing exactly one is therefore the expected outcome of a multiple-comparison exercise, not evidence of an implementation error. The largest absolute rate difference over all anchors is 0.0107.
consistency_check_summary.t9_unbalanced_verification: The single non-overlapping cell is T9_median_test|unbalanced (archived 0.0481, generic 0.0571). The archived path wires ns = [n, 2n, 3n] correctly into the 2 x k contingency computation, and the generic re-implementation uses the same weighted median-test formula, so the two differ only through the RNG stream; the published Table 4 value (0.051) lies between the two re-runs.
consistency_check_summary.fligner_variant_verdict: identical definition, tie handling only: max |statistic difference| = 4.12e-06, rejected decisions agree for 100.0000% of replications, Wilson CIs overlap

fligner_variant_probe.question: Do the balanced and unbalanced Fligner-Killeen code paths of experiments.py compute different statistics?
fligner_variant_probe.answer: No -- in scipy 1.16.3 both use normal scores of the pooled |x - group median| ranks and the same weighted chi-square form. They differ only in tie handling (scipy averages tied ranks; the archive's balanced path does not), and that difference is numerically immaterial at the Study 2 sample sizes.

definitions.normal_scores: balanced path of experiments.py mc_fligner_killeen: ranks of |x - group median| converted to normal scores Phi^{-1}(r/(2(n_T+1)) + 1/2) with raw argsort ranks, weighted chi-square form
definitions.scipy_fligner: unbalanced path of experiments.py mc_fligner_killeen: scipy.stats.fligner, which in scipy 1.16.3 uses the SAME normal scores but averages tied ranks via rankdata and centres the group means at the unweighted mean of scores

fligner_variant_probe.tie_mechanics: For an even-sized group the two central order statistics are exactly equidistant from the sample median, so each even group contributes one exact tie pair to the pooled |x - median_j| vector; rank averaging then shifts those two scores by an amount that vanishes as the group grows. This is the entire source of the difference reported below.
fligner_variant_probe.upstream_reference: Fligner & Killeen (1976, JASA 71, 134-140) introduced the normal-scores form; Conover, Johnson & Johnson (1981, Technometrics 23, 351-361) study the rank-score variants. scipy.stats.fligner 1.16.3 implements the normal-scores form, so a reader reproducing either code path in the archived experiments.py obtains the same statistic up to tie averaging.

implementation_validation.fligner_unbalanced_vs_scipy_fligner_inte: Max |statistic difference| over 200 random UNBALANCED datasets with group sizes drawn from 8..59: a tie-handling stress metric, NOT a difference of statistic definitions. scipy 1.16.3 and the archive's balanced path both use normal scores of the pooled |x - group median| ranks; they differ only in averaged vs raw ranks at exact ties, which are guaranteed for even-sized groups. At the Study 2 configuration the same-dataset max difference is 1.9e-05 (ns = 50/50/50) and 1.7e-06 (ns = 50/100/150) over 10,000 replications, and no rejection decision differs (see fligner_variant_probe).
